D8·sy2e — 2026-09-16
rule: A suggestion carries the 2.2 trust numbers of the detector that produced it, names no cause and proposes no change; approval binds to the candidate hash and is refused once the evidence set moves.
chose: 2.3 contract, settled before code. (1) A SUGGESTION IS A LOSS ROW, never a fix: {candidate hash, signal, scope = one initiative, evidence ids, count, corpus cutoff, engine version, detector report version, trust}. It names no cause and proposes no change; the fix, its predicted gain, its falsifier and its budget belong to Phase 3. (2) TRUST TRAVELS WITH IT: a candidate can only come from a detector the 2.2 protocol marked TRUSTED, and it carries that verdict's numbers (precision, recall, judged n, protocol and verdict event ids) so a reader sees how often this signal is right without leaving the row. Today that is `corrections` alone. (3) THE HASH IS THE EVIDENCE: sha256 over canonical {version, signal, scope, sorted evidence ids} — not the cutoff, not prose, not a branch. New evidence means a new candidate; a rejected candidate stays suppressed until its evidence set changes, which is exactly when its hash does. (4) APPROVAL BINDS TO THE EXACT CANDIDATE: approve, reject and revert re-derive candidates from the current log and refuse when the hash is no longer derivable, naming the hash that replaced it. Revert is a new event that ends an approval; nothing is erased or rewritten. (5) SURFACES: `sofar suggest [slug|--all] --dry-run [--json]` derives and prints, writing nothing; persistence is always an explicit verb — `suggest record|approve|reject|revert <hash>`; `suggest list` shows every candidate with its full history. `sofar tune` stays detection-only. No MCP tool and no digest section: the operator asks for suggestions, they are never pushed into every session's context. (6) MINIMUM EVIDENCE 3 instances in scope — one correction is ordinary work, a cluster is a pattern — and at most 10 open candidates per initiative. (7) PROTECTED FLOOR: the set of things a suggestion may ever change is today EMPTY (a loss row changes nothing), and log integrity, session routing, standing constraints, evaluator integrity, permissions and release policy are never in it. (8) Offline replay (context size, information preservation) is DEFERRED with a rule, because no trusted detector yields a candidate that changes injected context: no candidate kind that changes what is injected may ship before that check exists.
over: Candidates that name a cause or a fix (2.1's rule 3 forbids the detector; inheriting it in the proposal would launder the same guess); one candidate per finding (27 rows in this repo's own record); hashing the cutoff (every new event would churn every hash and defeat rejection suppression); a digest section or an MCP tool for suggestions (r1-fixes 2.1/2.4 are cutting injected bytes and tool schemas); building the replay check now against no candidate that needs it.
because: The audit's S5 asks for a complete lifecycle with immutable references, approval bound to the exact evaluated candidate, stale applies refused, suppression of rejected equivalents, minimum evidence and a protected floor. A loss row is what the trusted detector can honestly support: `corrections` proves that the record was fixed N times, not why, and 2.2 measured that it misses half of them — a number that belongs on the row the operator reads. Phase 3 consumes approved rows, which is what 3.4 ("first manual cycle on one round-1 loss row") needs from Phase 2.
